descriptionAdvanced.en: Rancagua is a historic city located in the heart of Chile's fertile central valley, about 90 kilometers south of Santiago. It is best known as the site of the 1814 Battle of Rancagua, a pivotal moment in the nation's struggle for independence. Today, the city is the center of Chile's rodeo culture, hosting the national championships every year in its massive arena. It also serves as the administrative hub for the massive El Teniente mine, the largest underground copper mine in the world. Surrounded by vineyards and orchards, Rancagua embodies the traditional agricultural and mining spirit of the O'Higgins Region.

en: The Medialuna Monumental de Rancagua is the primary venue for the National Rodeo Championship.
Located near the El Teniente copper mine, which began operations in the early 20th century.
The Battle of Rancagua is often called the 'Disaster of Rancagua' because of the patriot defeat.
The city center is designed in a 'damasco' (checkerboard) pattern typical of colonial Spanish planning.
The nearby thermal springs of Cauquenes have been visited by historical figures like Bernardo O'Higgins.
